tools.name: consult_council
tools.description: Ask the AI council to review the timeline. Five specialists check the real clips, frame by frame: the Animator (dead stretches with no designed motion, motion density, static or linear graphics), the Director (jump cuts, locked-off shots, almost-centred or unsafe placement, balance, rhythm, letterboxing), the Audio Guru (music bed, ducking, fades, silent graphic entrances, loud SFX, clipping, cuts off the beat, dead air) and the Researcher (sources behind the plan, watermarked / social / unlicensed files on the timeline, credits owed), plus the Comedian on @funny edits (every meme has a sourced why and lands on the punchline, no repeats, fresh memes, no dead zones over 8 s, the roast Edit DNA band). Each note has a severity: block (verify_edit_workflow refuses until fixed), fix, or note. Call it after building each pass and before verify_edit_workflow; fix every block and fix it lists.

compId.description: Comp to review; the active comp by default.

tools.name: find_free_media
tools.description: The Researcher's library search: licence-clear stills, video and audio with no watermark, from Openverse (CC0 / CC BY / CC BY-SA, commercial use allowed), Wikimedia Commons and NASA (public domain). Every result carries its licence and credit line. Search in PLAN (download false) to plan shots; download in GATHER with `download: true` and `pick` (result indices) — files land in a Research folder with their licence recorded, and `sceneIndex` attaches them to the plan. Prefer this over scraping arbitrary pages.

query.description: What to find, in plain words (e.g. 'city skyline night', 'ocean waves').

download.description: Download and import the picks (GATHER phase).

pick.description: Indices of the results to download; the top results when omitted.

sceneIndex.description: Plan scene the first download belongs to.

tools.name: spawn_subagent
tools.description: Spawn an autonomous AI sub-worker that runs in parallel. The subagent has access to all Bhippi tools and works independently on the given task, seeing the same project summary. Give it a council `role` to make it one of the five specialists: `researcher` (deep sourced research + licence-clear, watermark-free downloads), `animator` (frame-by-frame, motion-graphic-heavy graphics), `audio` (mix engineer / music producer: levels, ducking, beat sync, SFX per frame), `director` (layout, symmetry, camera angles, shot rhythm), `comedian` (@funny: memes that echo the punchline, receipts, comic timing). Returns immediately with a subagent ID; the subagent's progress and results appear in the chat's agent map. Max 6 concurrent subagents per turn.

task.description: Clear, actionable task description for the subagent. Be specific about what to do and what success looks like.

label.description: Short label for the agent map UI (e.g. 'Research B-roll', 'Generate lower-third', 'Process audio').

model.description: Optional model override for this subagent. Defaults to the parent turn's model.

maxRounds.description: Maximum tool call rounds (default 30). Lower = faster/cheaper, higher = more thorough.

role.description: Optional council seat the worker takes: its brief leads the worker's instructions.

tools.name: wait_subagent
tools.description: Block until a specific subagent finishes (or all if no ID given). Returns the subagent's final status and summary. Use when you need a subagent's output before continuing.

subagentId.description: The subagent ID to wait for. Omit to wait for all subagents of this turn.

tools.name: list_subagents
tools.description: List all subagents spawned by this turn with their current status (running, done, failed), elapsed time, and tool call count.

tools.name: attach_production_asset
tools.description: GATHER phase: records that a planned shot now has its media (when a generation or download ran without sceneIndex). Give sceneIndex (0-based) and optionally shotIndex, or kind 'music' for the music bed.

tools.name: finish_gathering
tools.description: GATHER phase: closes gathering once every planned shot, the voice-over and the music have real asset ids and no generation job is running. Missing music is composed and missing picture shots get a designed background plate automatically before the check, so nothing goes into editing empty. Fails with the missing list otherwise. After it succeeds, END YOUR TURN; the user presses Start editing.

acceptMissing.description: Only with the user's agreement: close with some shots dropped.

tools.name: compose_music
tools.description: Composes a bespoke music bed in about a second with Bhippi's own synthesiser (no generator needed): drums, pumping sub, pad, arp, a riser into each drop, mastered to about -14 LUFS. Its exact beat grid is stored, so snap_cuts_to_beats needs no analysis. Planning/gathering: attaches as the production's music; editing: laid on a free audio track, faded. Use it whenever there is no music or generation failed.

mood.description: energetic (launches, showreels; a drop) | chill (vlogs, tutorials) | cinematic (documentary, trailers) | corporate (SaaS, brand) | playful (fun, food, memes) | dark (tension) — or words ("upbeat corporate").

duration.description: Seconds (default: the timeline, or the plan target).

drops.description: Seconds from its start where it drops (snapped to the bar).

accents.description: Seconds for a crash: your cuts.

place.description: Lay it on the timeline (default only while editing).

db.description: Placed level (-6 alone; -18 under a voice).

tools.name: make_background
tools.description: Renders a slowly moving background plate for the frame so graphics never sit on flat black: glow (dark stage, breathing glow), gradient (drifting colours), paper (riso stock), grain (flat colour, grain). Brand colours unless given. Editing: laid on V1 under everything; gathering: imported to attach.

tools.name: build_edit_from_brief
tools.description: Builds a whole motion edit from a short brief in ONE call — the reliable way to make a video from scratch. You give the beats (what each one says) and the feel; Bhippi picks the template for each beat, holds each one long enough to read on the music's beat grid inside the genre's pacing, chooses transitions with their sound effects, composes a score that drops on the big beat with a crash on every cut, lays a designed background plate under it (when there is no footage), and saves the storyboard. Afterwards run run_frame_qa, fix what it lists, then judge_edit and verify_edit_workflow. Prefer it to building scenes, keyframes and sound one by one.

beats.description: 1–16 beats in order. One idea per beat; headlines of 2–7 words read best.

text.description: The headline (for a stat: its label; for a lower-third: the name).

kind.description: Guessed when left out: value → stat, points → list, "?" → question, cta or last → end, first → title. steps = numbered points.

accentWord.description: The word set in the accent colour.

value.description: stat: the number that counts up, e.g. "87" or "2.5".

hold.description: Seconds, only to override the planned reading time.

mood.description: energetic | chill | cinematic | corporate | playful | dark, or words ("upbeat, techy"). Sets the music, the transitions and the background.

genre.description: motion | saas | documentary | meme | edit | shorts … — the pacing it is held to; inferred when left out.

targetSeconds.description: Stretch the beats towards this length (never below reading time).

music.description: false to skip the music (default: compose one, or use the gathered music).

background.description: false to skip the background plate.

tools.name: run_frame_qa
tools.description: POLISH pass over the whole timeline or a range (the in/out selection, or start/end): samples it (every scene start plus every `step` seconds) and measures where every motion-scene layer rests (nested "[Motion]" comps included), every HTML graphic, title and caption, every footage or still reduced to a card or picture-in-picture, and the rotoscoped subject. Reports: anything off the frame or outside the safe area, graphics covering the face/hands, graphic-on-graphic and caption collisions, black frame edges, and — from rendered frames with the motion graphics drawn in — blank frames (flat white from a light stage, empty black, one flat colour). Each problem once, with its time range and the fix. Returns contact frames for you to look at. verify_edit_workflow requires a clear pass after your last edit.

times.description: Explicit timeline times instead of the automatic sample.

start.description: Timeline seconds the review starts (default 0, or the in point with selection).

end.description: Timeline seconds the review ends (default the end, or the out point with selection).

selection.description: Review only the in/out selection of the comp.

frames.description: Frames to render across the range for the blank-frame check (default 12, 0–24).

genre.description: Also report pacing against this genre's measured timing (advice only).

tools.name: review_frames
tools.description: Reviews the edit the way good films are made: frames at every cut, graphic landing, sound cue and marker, plus strips 0.06 s apart across the joins, as contact sheets you look at, and measured checks (murky frames, the same phrase on screen twice, cuts off the beat, sound cues buried under the music, an end card that leaves too soon, reading size). Changes nothing; fix what it lists, then review again.

at.description: Which frames: the moments things happen, the joins, or both (default).

times.description: Timeline seconds to look at instead (up to 24).

tools.name: organize_bin
tools.description: File every loose Project-bin entry into its category folder: Footage, B-roll, Motion Graphics ([MOGRT] and graphics-only comps), Generated, Backgrounds, Images, Music, SFX, Voice-over, Audio, Graphics. Reuses existing folders with matching names. Entries already in a folder are left alone. Anything you import, download, generate or build is filed automatically; use this to tidy a bin that was filled before.

tools.name: fill_background
tools.description: Put a background behind picture that no longer fills the frame — a shot scaled down ("zoom out"), moved aside, cropped, rotated, or a vertical clip in a wide comp — which otherwise renders black at the edges. Finds every such span itself (or only those in start–end) and places the background on a track under the shot, adding one below it if needed. source 'auto' (default): a background from the project library (an image or video whose name or bin says bg, background, backdrop, plate, texture or wallpaper), otherwise a blurred, darkened, full-frame copy of the same shot, otherwise a colour matte in the plan palette. Edit results warn when a change leaves black edges; call this then.

compId.description: Comp to fix (defaults to the active comp)

end.description: Only fill up to this time (seconds)

source.description: 'auto' (library, then blurred shot, then colour), 'blur', 'color', or an asset id from the library

color.description: Hex colour for source 'color' (defaults to the plan palette)

tools.name: layout_clip
tools.description: Reframes footage with a weighted, exporting move: presenter to the left/right 55% (slot left-55 / right-55, a 52% card inside the safe area) so a side-panel or teaching-card can take the 35% column on the other side, picture-in-picture corners (pip-bottom-right …, inside the safe area), centre-small, or back to full. Animates scale/x/y with ease-out over `duration` seconds starting at `at`, and optionally returns at `until`. Every slot keeps the picture inside the safe margins.

at.description: Timeline seconds the move starts (default clip start).

until.description: Timeline seconds to move back to the previous framing.

tools.name: split_screen
tools.description: Shows 2–4 clips at once in a split screen that suits the comp's shape: stacked top/bottom in 9:16 and feed frames, side by side in 16:9 (layout auto), or a 2×2 grid, three-up, or a picture-in-picture inset. Each clip is cropped to its cell and fills it edge to edge (focus keeps a face in frame). The clips must be on separate video tracks and overlap in time. Returns the cells and where the captions belong (on the seam of a stack).

ratio.description: Share of the first cell: 0.5 even (two people), 0.4 facecam over gameplay / B-roll, 0.6 for a lead guest.

corner.description: PiP corner (default top-left in tall frames, clear of the button rail; bottom-right in wide ones).

pipSize.description: PiP width as a share of the frame width (default 0.3 tall, 0.28 wide).

focus.description: Per clip, the point of the source (0–1) to keep in the middle of its cell, e.g. the speaker's face.

tools.name: seamless_transition
tools.description: A dynamic cut that does not read as a transition: push (outgoing pushes 6% while the incoming settles from 6%, with a push-left blend), zoom-punch (12% + cross-zoom), blur-push, occluder (a Crimson ribbon card sweeps over the cut), or cut (sound only). Adds a whoosh 0.25 s before the cut unless whoosh:false. Put it on a beat (snap_cuts_to_beats first).

title.description: occluder only: chapter title on the card.

tools.name: analyze_music_beats
tools.description: Detects tempo and beat times of a music asset from its waveform (onset envelope → autocorrelation tempo → beat grid). Stores bpm and beats on the production's music. Beat times are source seconds.

tools.name: analyze_song
tools.description: Maps a song: beats, bars, drops, hits and each lyric word's time. In one call: tempo, beats, bars, 4-bar phrases, drops, the hits worth an accent, and, given the lyrics, every word with its time (the lead vocal is separated so sung lines are heard; words the engine misses are placed between heard ones and marked *), grouped into lines and sections from [Section] headers, plus cut points (section starts on bars, line starts, bars). Times are source seconds of the song. Saves the full map as a research note. Use it before planning any edit timed to music with words.

lyrics.description: The words as the user gave them, one line per line; [Verse 1] style headers name sections.

vocal.description: Separate the lead vocal before transcribing (default true; false for plain speech).

transcribe.description: Default true. False: beats and structure only, lyrics spread by length.

tools.name: snap_cuts_to_beats
tools.description: Moves every video cut and overlay entrance within `tolerance` seconds onto the nearest music beat. A cut between two clips is rolled (the outgoing end and the incoming start move together; linked audio stays, so it becomes a J/L split), so no gaps are created; an edge beside a gap is trimmed and overlays are moved; nothing overlaps. Uses the plan's analysed music placed on the timeline, or explicit beats in timeline seconds.

grid.description: Snap to every beat (default), every bar line, or every 4-bar phrase line (where big world changes land).

tools.name: level_audio
tools.description: Measures every dialogue and music clip with EBU R128 and sets clip gain so dialogue sits at targetLufs (default −16) and the music bed musicBedDb under it (default −20 dB, i.e. −36 LUFS). Reports measured → target per clip and true-peak warnings. Follow with score_audio_clip for ducking under dense phrases.

tools.name: erase_subject_clip
tools.description: Magic eraser: removes the rotoscoped subject from a clip and returns a clean background plate (temporal median of uncovered pixels + LaMa inpainting of what was always covered, composited per frame). Requires rotoscope_clip first and the Magic eraser model installed (install_local_model task 'erase'). With replaceBackground (default true) it swaps the 'Original background' layer of a behind-subject sandwich for the plate, so text and graphics sit truly behind the person with no ghost. Waits for the job.

mode.description: clean-plate for a static camera (fast, stable); per-frame for a moving camera (slow).

refine.description: LaMa on the seam band each frame.

tools.name: reveal_subject
tools.description: A reveal moment on the rotoscoped subject. Default style `cells` (the reference opening): the subject appears out of the clean plate through hot accent-coloured cells cut from their own roto matte, seeded at the face and cascading down the body, cooling to the real footage — a GPU motion scene placed above the clip (optional `title` words sit behind the subject, `phrase` lands under the face). Legacy styles: `cubes` (a tile grid falls over the frame while the subject fades in) and `wipe`. For the full hook with frame-to-card use create_motion_scene template subject-reveal.

title.description: cells: up to two words either side of the face, behind the subject.

phrase.description: cells: a short phrase that lands word by word under the face.

tools.name: list_motion_templates
tools.description: Lists the motion-engine templates (After Effects-grade scenes rendered on the GPU, identical in preview and export): id, what it is for and its length. query with a template id (or a word that matches 8 or fewer) to get its params and technique ids. Use before create_motion_scene.

tools.name: list_character_actions
tools.description: Lists the characters you can cast — the user's own character LIBRARY first (characters they saved in the Characters window, then its 20 examples), and the three built-in rigs (dome-kid, shape-buddy, flat-corporate) — plus every action and expression they all perform.

tools.name: list_characters
tools.description: Shows the user's character library: the characters they saved in the Characters window (2D and 3D share one library), then its 20 examples, each with a one-line look (age, body, hair, clothes, extras), plus the spec format for a new design. Call it before casting any character and cast from it with create_character {"character":"<name>"}.

query.description: Only characters whose name or look mentions this (e.g. "kid", "blazer", "senior").

full.description: Return every full spec (to copy one for a new design).

tools.name: create_character
tools.description: Places an animated character performing timed actions (walk, hop, leap, wave, point, talk, celebrate, surprise, facepalm…); blinks and idles are automatic. Library characters use smooth motion or their saved 24/12 fps drawing cadence; built-in rigs default to on twos. CAST FROM THE USER'S CHARACTER LIBRARY FIRST: `character` is the name of a character they saved in the Characters window or one of its examples (list_characters shows who is there and how each looks); library characters are hand-drawn 2.5D people that turn toward where they walk and look. Use `look` for small changes (clothes in brand colours, a hat) so the character stays theirs. Only when the user asks for something specific the library cannot give, design a new character with `spec` (the library's format; save:true adds it to their library). The built-in rigs dome-kid (flat dome head, hoodie), shape-buddy (round creature with googly eyes) and flat-corporate (office worker) are only for when the user asks for that style. Stands with its feet at `at`, `height` px tall. Into an existing motion scene with clipId, or as its own scene on the timeline.

character.description: A library character's name (saved or example, from list_characters), or a built-in rig: dome-kid, shape-buddy, flat-corporate. With spec, the new character's name.

at.description: Scene px of the point between its feet (default bottom centre).

height.description: Standing height in px (default half the frame).

t.description: Start, in scene seconds (a number, e.g. 1.5).

to.description: point/look: [x, y] scene px. walk/sneak/run/leap: a scene x, [x, y], or a number of px.

actions.description: Timed actions [{t (scene s), do, duration?, to?, hand?, text?, words?, expression?, amount?}]. do: idle, wave, point, look, hop, leap, walk, sneak, run, celebrate, shrug, nod, shake, facepalm, surprise, think, type, talk, expression, turn. point/look to [x,y] scene px; walk/sneak/run/leap to a scene x or [x,y] (or a number of px); talk with text (or lip_sync_character); expression: normal|happy|sad|wide|determined|closed|unsure|side.

palette.description: Built-in rigs only: {skin, top, bottom, shoe, hair, accent, eye, pupil, mouth} colours (e.g. brand colours on the hoodie). For library characters use look.

facing.description: 1 right, -1 left (library characters turn three-quarters that way; walking turns them).

step.description: Optional legacy 30 fps drawing-step override: 1 = ones, 2 = twos, 3 = threes. Omit for library characters to use their saved Smooth/24/12 fps timing; built-in rigs default to 2.

clipId.description: Add into this motion scene instead of a new one.

look.description: Changes laid onto a library character, in its spec format, e.g. {"top":{"kind":"hoodie","color":"#F6A623"},"acc":["headphones"]}.

spec.description: A new character in the library format (list_characters specFormat; copy an example with list_characters full:true and change it). Only when nothing in the library fits a specific request.

save.description: With spec: also save the new character to the user's library (it needs a name).

tools.name: animate_character
tools.description: Adds (or with replace:true, replaces) timed actions on a character layer in a motion scene.

t.description: Start, in scene seconds (a number, e.g. 1.5).

to.description: point/look: [x, y] scene px. walk/sneak/run/leap: a scene x, [x, y], or a number of px.

actions.description: Timed actions [{t (scene s), do, duration?, to?, hand?, text?, words?, expression?, amount?}]. do: idle, wave, point, look, hop, leap, walk, sneak, run, celebrate, shrug, nod, shake, facepalm, surprise, think, type, talk, expression, turn. point/look to [x,y] scene px; walk/sneak/run/leap to a scene x or [x,y] (or a number of px); talk with text (or lip_sync_character); expression: normal|happy|sad|wide|determined|closed|unsure|side.

tools.name: lip_sync_character
tools.description: Makes a character's mouth follow the voice-over: the transcribed words under the scene (or from–to within it) become timed mouth shapes.

tools.name: check_pacing
tools.description: Pacing QA: measures the edit the way the reference films were measured and compares it with a target. It checks how often something new happens (foreground swaps), entrance speed, whether text holds long enough to read, typing speed by purpose (fields vs lines read with the voice-over), and cuts on the beat against chance. Target: a genre's measured pacing (genre: saas-explainer, ai-launch, brand-identity-film, kinetic-type, 2.5d-tricks), or a reference's own pacingTarget from analyze_reference_video.

target.description: {swapGap: [min,max] s, entrance: [min,max] frames, readingWps?, beatSync?, eases?}; usually analyze_reference_video's motion.pacingTarget.

beats.description: Beat times (timeline s) from analyze_music_beats, to score cuts on the beat.

tools.name: import_lottie
tools.description: Places a Lottie animation the user supplied (.json or .lottie file, or its library assetId) as a motion scene. The common subset (shapes, paths, keyed transforms with their eases, fills, strokes, gradients, trim paths, merge paths, parenting, precomps) becomes real editable layers that match lottie-web; files that use anything else (animated paths, masks, mattes, text, images, effects, expressions…) are rendered frame by frame with alpha instead, so every file plays. Bhippi never searches or downloads LottieFiles content (their licence forbids it): the user downloads the file and gives it to you.

mode.description: auto (default): native layers when the file allows, otherwise rendered frames.

width.description: On-screen width in px (default 60% of the frame height's worth).

loop.description: Rendered files: repeat for the whole scene.

clipId.description: Add into this motion scene (at scene time t) instead of a new one.

tools.name: add_fx
tools.description: Drops a motion accent into a motion scene (clipId, at scene time t) or over the timeline as its own overlay (start): confetti-pop (a burst that falls), confetti-rain, sparkles, burst (lines from a point), ripple (rings), star-glint (a lens star, for glass, logos and product edges), glow-ring, speed-lines, exclaim (comic "!" marks), gradient-border (a moving gradient outline around a target layer or box), echo (trailing copies of a moving target layer), and ambient dust, bokeh, snow, embers, light-shafts, mesh-gradient or dot-wave. Call it with no kind to list them.

clipId.description: A motion scene / [Motion] comp to add into; leave out to place an overlay on the timeline.

size.description: px (glint, ring, burst reach, sparkle radius) or a multiplier for particles.

box.description: gradient-border without a target: [x, y, w, h].

direction.description: speed-lines: degrees the streaks travel (0 = right, 180 = left).

tools.name: list_transitions
tools.description: Lists the motion-design transitions create_motion_sequence joins beats with (whip, zoom-through, blur-bridge, z-recede, card-zoom-reveal, shape wipes, eyelids, swap-when-hidden, snaps, world trucks…) and what each does.

tools.name: create_motion_sequence
tools.description: Builds several beats into ONE motion scene joined by motion-design transitions, the way SaaS and brand films flow instead of cutting between clips. A beat is {template, params} (list_motion_templates), {ui: {…create_ui_screen arguments}}, {scene} (a raw scene) or {clipId} (an existing motion clip), each with optional hold (seconds it owns the frame) and name. layout "cuts" replaces beats in place through the transitions; "world" lays them out on one canvas and trucks a camera between them, so the background never cuts. A guide (dot, orb, sparkle or ring) can travel from beat to beat as the continuity object. Beats' sound cues move with them, and each transition adds its whoosh, swish or impact. Places one layered [Motion] comp; returns each beat's start and each cut in timeline seconds.

beats.description: [{template, params, hold?, name?} | {ui:{kind, content, actions, …}, hold?} | {scene, hold?} | {clipId, hold?}]

transitions.description: One per join: a kind or {kind, duration?, direction?: left|right|up|down, glyph?: circle|square|rounded|star|diamond, mode?: out|in, at?: [x,y], to?: [x,y], strength?, color?, twist?}. Kinds: cut, dissolve, push, slide, whip, zoom-through, blur-bridge, z-recede, card-zoom-reveal, shape-wipe, iris, diagonal-wipe, noise-dissolve, white-out, black-breath, palette-swap-cut, eyelid, scale-cut, snap-punch, snap-zoom-out, snap-press, swap-when-hidden, collapse-into, spin, glitch, light-leak, truck, camera-match, glow-handoff, flash-bridge.

guide.description: {shape?: dot|orb|sparkle|ring, color?, size?, stops: [{beat: index, at: [x,y] frame px, t?: seconds into the beat, size?}], end?: fade|stay}

background.description: A colour under everything that never cuts; templates then draw no stage of their own.

tools.name: capture_product_ui
tools.description: Screenshots the user's real product (a web page or web app URL) in a headless browser at 2×, and shows it to you with a 100 px grid. Then animate it with create_ui_screen {screenshot, width, height, parts:[{id, box:[x,y,w,h], radius?, text?}], actions}: the parts are cut out of the screenshot and can be clicked, lifted, typed into (give text for fields), counted, dragged and zoomed into like any UI screen.

theme.description: Ask the page for its dark scheme.

tools.name: capture_app_session
tools.description: Captures a live product as parts in states, crisp at 3x: plays a short session in a headless browser (click, hover, type, key, wait) and captures each named part in each state; typing with a part is captured after every character. No url = Bhippi itself, from the real app state, with named parts @composer @field @send @pills @menu @chat @messages @timeline @program @source @project. Checks resolution and fonts; a repeat capture is reused. Parts land in AI Work/ui-parts/<name> with manifest.json.

url.description: The product page (http/https). Leave out to capture Bhippi itself.

steps.description: In order. {do:"click"|"hover", selector} · {do:"type", selector, text, part?, partSelector?} · {do:"key", key} · {do:"wait", ms} · {do:"eval", js} · {do:"capture", part, selector, state?, pad?}. Selectors are CSS, or @name for Bhippi parts.

ready.description: A selector the page is ready when it shows.

reuse.description: Reuse an identical earlier capture (default true).

images.description: Attach a contact sheet of the parts (default true).

tools.name: create_product_demo
tools.description: Makes a captured app session into a product demo of editable layers. From a capture_app_session capture: the camera lands close on named parts and pulls back to the whole window tilted in 3D; named cursors (you, bhippi, claude, gpt, gemini, local) travel on arcs, click with a ring and type; each part shows its captured state on the frame (typing plays over a span or word by word). template "window-explode": the parts float apart in depth and slam back on slam. Times are seconds from the demo start. Places a layered [Motion] comp with sound cues; update_motion_scene params rebuild it with new times.

capture.description: The capture_app_session name (its folder in AI Work/ui-parts) or its manifest.json path.

shots.description: Where the camera lands at `at`: {at, focus: part, fill?} close on a part (fill of the frame, default 0.7; the frame stays on the app where it can, centre: true aims dead centre) or {at, wide: true} the whole window tilted (fill 0.84); optional tilt [rx, ry] and move (seconds of travel).

actions.description: {at, click: part, cursor?} · {at, hover: part, cursor?} · {at, type: part, until?, words?: [seconds each word lands], text?, cursor?} plays its typing states · {at, set: {part, state}} swaps to a captured state.

cursors.description: Named cursors: you, bhippi, claude, gpt, gemini, local, or {id, label, color}. The first clicks when an action names none.

explode.description: {at, slam, depth?, spread?, blur?}: the window comes apart in depth from at and slams back together on slam.

template.description: window-explode: the exploded-window move alone (give at and slam).

stage.description: light, grid, cool, dark, none, or a colour (default: picked per film).

tilt.description: The wide shot tilt [rx, ry] in degrees.

variant.description: Another look: tilt side, stage and explode pattern.

tools.name: list_ui_kinds
tools.description: Lists the ready-made UI screens for create_ui_screen (search, chat, dashboard, table, form, phone notifications, kanban, pricing) with their content fields and part names, and the action types.

tools.name: create_ui_screen
tools.description: A living product UI for SaaS / app explainers: a screen (ready-made kind, or your own HTML) in a browser, phone or laptop frame that the scene types into, clicks, hover-lifts, sweeps, counts, highlights, drags, switches pages on and zooms into, with a gliding cursor and UI sounds. Rendered once to crisp pictures (2×) and animated by the GPU motion engine, so preview and export match; it opens as a layered [Motion] comp. Time actions to the voice-over (typing lands with the words). Returns the part names.

tools.name: list_3d_presets
tools.description: Lists the headless-Blender 3D presets (glossy pearl orb, crystal lit by a gradient world, device hero, extruded logo word, letters dropping) and whether Blender is installed on this machine. Call before render_3d_scene.

tools.name: render_3d_scene
tools.description: Renders real 3D in the user's own Blender, headless in the background (glass, pearl, metal, gems, extruded type, soft floor shadows, depth of field, motion blur), and places the result as a [Motion] comp: a PNG sequence with alpha that composites like footage (mattes, effects, 2D layers on top). Give a `preset` from list_3d_presets with `params`, or a raw `scene` {objects:[{id,kind,position,rotation,scale,material:{preset,color},positionKeys,rotationKeys,scaleKeys,parent}],world,lights,camera:{position,target,lens,fstop,positionKeys,targetKeys}} in Blender axes (x right, y away from camera, z up, metres; keys {t,v,ease} with named or cubic-bezier eases). Draft quality (EEVEE, about 0.7 s a 1080p frame) while designing; quality "final" (Cycles on the GPU, about 3 s a frame) before export. It waits for the render; if the turn ends first, place it later with {jobId}. camera.json and objects2d.json beside the frames give the camera move and each object's screen box per frame for 2D layers that must track it. Objects can carry pictures: material {preset:'image', image:<path>} on a 'plane' (device-hero screenImage and card-ring images put real UI screens from create_ui_screen, or captures, into 3D). An 'empty' is an invisible pivot to parent and spin groups.

preset.description: pearl-core-orb | crystal-gradient-env | device-hero | logo-extrude | letters-drop | card-ring | sphere-bouquet

scene.description: A raw 3D scene, or overrides merged over the preset (world, camera, lights, objects).

quality.description: draft = EEVEE (fast), final = Cycles GPU path tracing.

start.description: Timeline seconds to place it at.

step.description: Render every Nth frame (2 halves a draft's time; plays at fps/N).

place.description: false: only render and return the footage layer to add to another scene.

jobId.description: Place a render that finished after an earlier turn ended.

waitMinutes.description: How long to wait for the render in this turn (default 20).

syncCamera.description: Default true: adds a motion-engine camera that moves exactly like Blender's, so layers set threeD sit in the render's space (a 3D layer at the camera target's depth keeps its size).

track.description: Object ids to follow: each becomes a null 'track-<id>' on its screen centre; parent labels, glints and callouts to it.

tools.name: motion_guide
tools.description: Motion-direction playbooks measured on professional reference films: beat recipes with durations, look, timing, rules, eases and engine features for a genre. Call with no topic for the list; call motion_guide {topic} before planning a SaaS explainer, AI launch, brand identity film, kinetic type, 2.5D piece, character story, hand-made (riso, crayon pen, cut-paper) film or the sound pass.

tools.description: The hand-made motion library: looks (riso print, crayon, ink, pencil, cut-paper, felt, scope), ink sets, every drawable item kind with its params (primitives, generative motifs, bot and sprite characters with faces, hand-writing, the pen tool, construction lines, scope traces), motion verbs (draw, fillIn, pop, boil, on twos), the riso/halftone effects, drawn templates and transitions, and a complete example `drawing` layer.
