tools.name: check_motion_arcs
tools.description: The animator's flip test on a motion scene: tracks the centre of every moving layer and named drawing item frame by frame (dot-to-dot) and reports moves in dead-straight lines (living things move on arcs), moves at one speed from start to stop (no slow-out/slow-in), one-frame jumps, and characters that change size while they travel (layout drift), each with the fix. Run it after building or editing an animated scene, fix with update_motion_scene (key arc/through/ease/easeAxes), and run again.

clipId.description: The motion clip, its [Motion] comp clip, a layer clip or the comp id.

tools.name: search_icons
tools.description: Finds Lucide icons (2,000+ line icons) by name words, e.g. "shield", "chart", "user plus". Use a result inside a shape layer's shape.groups as {"kind":"icon","icon":"<name>","iconSize":120,"color":"#fff","position":[x,y]}; it becomes real vector paths you can trim (draw on), scale and recolour.

query.description: Words in the icon name.

tools.name: svg_to_shape
tools.description: Turns an SVG (a logo, icon or illustration file, or svg markup) into a vector shape tree for a motion scene shape layer: {groups, bounds}. Place it as {"type":"shape","shape":{"shape":"path","groups":…,"bounds":…}} to animate, trim, recolour or scale it losslessly.

fit.description: [width, height] px box to scale it into.

tools.name: create_motion_scene
tools.description: Places a GPU motion scene on its own track above the footage, opened as a layered "[Motion]" comp: each layer (stage, titles, subject, phrase, panels, cards) is its own clip on its own track, the way After Effects shows a comp, so the user can open it and move, trim, hide, restack or restyle any layer — and it still renders as one scene, exactly as the template built it. The engine: After Effects-style layers with keyframes (bezier eases, expressions), 3D layers and camera, parenting, masks, track mattes, blend modes, motion blur, glow/blur/glass/halation/duotone/pixel-sort/zoom-blur effects, text animators that land word by word, and matte effects cut from a roto matte (subject-reveal, matte-fill). Give a `template` (list_motion_templates) with `params`, or a raw `scene` {version:1,width,height,duration,layers:[…]}. Footage params take {"clipId"} of a timeline clip — its asset, source time and roto matte are filled in. subject-reveal/big-number-behind need rotoscope_clip first and use the clean plate from erase_subject_clip when one exists. Every scene is fitted to the safe area (panels and type never rest off the frame). Over a background plate on the timeline (a clip named background/gradient/backdrop/plate), full-frame brand templates draw no stage of their own, so the plate shows instead of a flat brand stage. The scene's sound cues are laid on audio tracks unless sfx is false. With a brand kit active every scene is built in the brand; prefer the brand-* templates (brand-title, brand-lower-third, brand-stat, brand-panel, brand-logo-sting, brand-end-card, brand-transition), which render the kit's guideline moves and layouts exactly. The result lists the layers with their clip ids.

params.description: Template params (see list_motion_templates). Footage params: {"clipId"} or {"assetId"}.

scene.description: A raw MotionScene instead of a template (src/motion/types.ts vocabulary).

sfx.description: Lay the scene's sound cues (default true).

nest.description: Default true: the scene lives in its own layered "[Motion]" comp (one clip per layer) placed on the timeline as one nested clip. false places the whole scene as a single clip directly on the timeline.

useBrand.description: Default true: with a brand kit active the scene is built in it (brand-* templates from its guideline; every other template recoloured, re-typed and re-timed to the brand). false keeps the house Crimson look.

fit.description: Default true: type, panels and cards that rest outside the safe area are moved (and shrunk if too big) back inside it. false leaves the layout exactly as given.

safeMargin.description: Safe margin as a fraction of the frame on every side (default: the editor safe area, 5% at the sides and 6% top and bottom; the storyboard may ask for 0.06).

tools.name: get_motion_scene
tools.description: Reads a motion scene. For a layered "[Motion]" comp: every layer with its clip id, track, time on the comp, text and whether it is hidden (precomps list their own layers and comp), the scene outline (types, effects, animated properties with key times), the template params it was built from, and any layer resting outside the safe area. full: true adds the whole scene JSON for precise edits.

clipId.description: The "[Motion]" comp clip on the timeline (what create_motion_scene returns as clipId), the comp id, any of its layer clips, or a single motion scene clip.

tools.name: update_motion_scene
tools.description: Edits a motion scene; on a layered "[Motion]" comp the change is written back layer by layer, keeping each layer's clip and track and the user's own moves, trims, hides and Motion changes. params: new template params (rebuilt from its template, e.g. new words, times, colours; clips nobody moved take the new timing). patches: [{layer, path, value}] set any layer property by dotted path — e.g. {layer:"title-left",path:"transform.position",value:{k:[{t:0,v:[400,300],ease:"expo-out"},{t:0.6,v:[480,300]}]}}, {layer:"subject",path:"effects.0.speed",value:0.8}, value null deletes (times are the layer's own seconds). addLayers: [layer | {layer, above|below: id}] (a new layer gets its own clip and track). removeLayers: [ids]. retime: factor (>1 slower). scene: replace fields of the scene. The result is fitted to the safe area unless fit is false.

clipId.description: The "[Motion]" comp clip on the timeline (what create_motion_scene returns as clipId), the comp id, any of its layer clips, or a single motion scene clip.

finish.description: The scene's finish adjustment layer: launch-light | launch-dark | {preset, exposure?, bloom?, vignette?, grain?, cardShadow?} | none.

fit.description: Default true: type, panels and cards that rest outside the safe area are moved (and shrunk if too big) back inside it. false leaves the layout exactly as given.

safeMargin.description: Safe margin as a fraction of the frame on every side (default: the editor safe area, 5% at the sides and 6% top and bottom; the storyboard may ask for 0.06).

tools.name: analyze_reference_video
tools.description: Learns a style from a reference film ("make my edits like this"): measures cuts, shot-length histogram, hook density and palette, keeps contact sheets (opening at 4 fps + whole film), and returns the sheets as images for you to study. Then call save_style_profile with what you saw (cadence, look, type, motion grammar, and which motion template each moment maps to). Local path or imported assetId; download URLs first. With the media Python set up it also returns a motion profile: cuts and hidden cuts (blur-bridge, white-out, black, whip), foreground swaps, move lengths with fitted eases matched to Bhippi's named eases, camera share, animation on twos, the music tempo, and how many cuts land on a beat against chance. It includes a pacingTarget for check_pacing.

motion.description: false skips the motion profile (hidden cuts, swaps, fitted eases, camera, tempo; needs the media Python).

maxSeconds.description: Seconds of the film to measure for the motion profile (default 180).

tools.name: save_style_profile
tools.description: Saves a style profile as the project's active guideline (loaded into the AI context for every later turn). profile: prose covering CADENCE (hook density, shot lengths, graphic every N s, chapter device), LOOK (palette, grade, depth), TYPE, MOTION GRAMMAR (eases, exits, motion blur, sound on every event) and a TEMPLATE MAP (moment → motion template). builtin: "motion-designer-explainer" loads the measured profile of the reference motion-design explainer (crimson stage, subject reveal hook, hex chapter roadmap, glass teaching cards, word-by-word type).

tools.name: track_motion
tools.description: Motion-tracks a video clip (OpenCV Lucas-Kanade with forward-backward checks, CPU): `points` [[x, y], ...] as frame fractions at `start`, and/or a `region` [x, y, w, h] for a planar track (position + scale + rotation of a surface such as a face, hand or phone screen). Returns samples in timeline seconds with confidence. With `apply` {motionClipId, layer, point? | planar: true, offset?: [dx, dy] px}, the samples become keyframes on that motion-scene layer so a callout, label or card follows the motion (parent other layers to it for groups).

tools.name: nest_motion_scenes
tools.description: Moves every motion scene placed directly on the comp's timeline into its own layered "[Motion] …" comp (AI Motion bin), one clip per layer, and leaves one nested clip at the same place and length. New scenes from create_motion_scene are layered already.

tools.name: split_motion_layers
tools.description: Opens "[Motion]" comps that still hold their scene as ONE clip into layers — one clip per layer on its own track, precomps as their own layered comps — in place: the comp keeps its id, so the timeline clips that nest it are untouched and it draws exactly as before. Use it on older motion comps so the user can see and change each layer. No ids: every such comp in the project.

compId.description: A "[Motion]" comp id, or the timeline clip that nests it.

tools.name: get_brand_guideline
tools.description: Reads the active brand kit's detailed guideline - the rules every graphic of this video follows: colour usage and stage, the type scale in px at 1080p, motion timing/easing/travel, the signature moves keyed frame by frame (title-in, word-cascade, title-out, lower-third-in/out, stat-count, emphasis, logo-sting, transition, end-card, caption-pop, background-drift), layouts per aspect ratio with zones, and scene recipes that map beats to brand-* motion templates. Read it before planning the edit and again before building graphics. Read-only, any phase.

id.description: Kit id or name; the active kit when omitted.

move.description: One move id: its full frame-by-frame keys.

aspect.description: Only the layouts for this aspect ratio.

tools.name: extract_brand_from_url
tools.description: Reads a brand off a website (the product or company URL the user gave): the colours its CSS paints with, weighted by use (brand/primary/accent variables, backgrounds, buttons, theme-color), the fonts it declares mapped to installed families, and logo candidates (inline SVG, logo images, icons). Returns candidates plus suggested create_brand_kit arguments. Use it first whenever the user gives a product link and has no kit. Read-only, any phase.

tools.name: check_brand_compliance
tools.description: Checks every graphic in the composition (and comps nested in it) against the active brand kit: colours outside the palette, fonts outside the type pairing, motion scenes not built in the brand. Run it before verify_edit_workflow and fix what it reports. Read-only, any phase.

id.description: Kit id or name; the active kit when omitted.

compId.description: Composition to check; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: train_brand_kit
tools.description: Saves what a reference taught into a brand kit (/train). Measure first: analyze_reference_video for videos and links (pass its id as referenceId: the measured cut rate and palette are added for you), extract_brand_from_url for websites, look at images. Then send 3–12 short rules, each {area: pacing|color|type|layout|motion|captions|audio|voice|do|dont, text: one rule (8–200 chars), value?: measured numbers or lists}. Rules another reference already taught are strengthened, not repeated.

tools.name: forget_training
tools.description: Undoes one /train: removes what a brand kit learned only from that source (sourceId from train_brand_kit).

tools.name: search_memes
tools.description: @funny meme brain: searches the local meme library (memes already explained and saved: a shipped seed plus every meme saved with save_meme) for a beat. It is a cache, not the whole internet: when nothing here fits the beat, or the user named a meme that is not here, use find_memes_online. Pass the punchline's concrete words as `echo` — the literal echo (the meme says or names the word the host just said: "zeher", "juice", "German shepherd") is the strongest match and the device that makes a meme land. Also matches names and aliases in English, Hinglish and Devanagari (ज़हर finds zeher/zahar), the meme's meaning, what is said in its clip, the comic intent, emotion, trend score and region. The video's audience decides which memes exist at all: viewers never get another country's local meme unless it crossed over, and their own country's memes come first. Every hit carries reasons, meaning, useWhen, dontUseWhen and its formats. Unverified memes are hidden unless includeUnverified. Read-only; any phase. Before placing a hit, check its dontUseWhen against the beat and write a one-line why; then fetch it with get_meme_media.

audience.description: Who the video is for: "global" (the English-speaking internet at large) or the viewers' country as a two-letter code (IN, US, GB, BR, MX, JP, KR, PH, NG, DE…). Default: the comp's audience (set on save_beat_sheet). Another country's local memes are left out unless they crossed over; the audience's own come first. "auto" uses the comp's.

query.description: Free text: a meme name, a topic or the beat's words (any script).

echo.description: Concrete words or short phrases from the beat a meme could repeat back (from the beat sheet's echo list), e.g. ["zeher"] or ["German shepherd"].

emotion.description: The emotion to hit (shock, sad, flex, cringe…).

region.description: Prefer memes from this region: global, a country code (IN, BR…) or any. Default: the audience's.

format.description: Prefer memes that have this format (e.g. clip for a cutaway with its own audio).

includeUnverified.description: Also return memes whose meaning has not been checked against a source (never auto-place those).

tools.name: find_memes_online
tools.description: @funny meme brain: searches the internet for memes that fit THIS video — one beat's context, or a meme the user asked for by name — as the video's viewers' own internet would answer: DuckDuckGo results for their country and language, Know Your Meme (each hit's About/Origin text read as `explainer`), Reddit search and YouTube via yt-dlp. Use it for every punchline beat worth a meme (search_memes first only as a cache of memes already explained), and always for a meme the user named (`named` true). For a non-English audience pass `localQuery`: the beat's idea in the viewers' language, the way their meme pages would say it. Returns candidates (name, provider, url, explainer, mediaUrls), problems (a failing source never fails the call) and libraryHits (library memes that match). Candidates are NOT library memes: read the explainer or page (scrape_web_page), check that the meme means what the beat needs and that this audience knows it, then save_meme (region: global or the country it is from) and get_meme_media. Read-only; any phase.

query.description: What the beat is about as a meme would say it, in a few English words ("pretending everything is fine", "caught lying on camera"), or the meme's exact name when named is true ("Distracted Boyfriend").

localQuery.description: The same idea in the audience's language, when that is not English ("se fazendo de sonso", "ばれた", "zeher de diya"). Searched first: that is where the local memes are.

echo.description: Concrete words from the beat a meme could say back (from the beat sheet's echo list).

named.description: True when the user asked for this meme by name: find that exact meme and its explainer, not something like it.

audience.description: Who the video is for: "global" (the English-speaking internet at large) or the viewers' country as a two-letter code (IN, US, GB, BR, MX, JP, KR, PH, NG, DE…). Default: the comp's audience (set on save_beat_sheet). Decides the search region and language.

compId.description: The comp whose audience to use (default: the open one).

tools.name: refresh_meme_trends
tools.description: @funny meme brain: what is trending right now, from Know Your Meme (newsfeed, with each entry's About/Origin text as `explainer`), Imgflip top templates, Reddit weekly top (r/IndianDankMemes, r/IndianMeyMeys, r/dankmemes, r/memes), YouTube searches via yt-dlp, and KLIPY / GIPHY trending when their keys are in the credential store. Answers the cached refresh when it is under 6 hours old (force:true refetches). It says what is trending in general, not what fits a beat: for that use find_memes_online. Returns candidates (name, provider, url, explainer, mediaUrls), per-provider counts, problems (a failing provider never fails the call) and libraryHits (library memes trending now). Candidates are NOT library memes: to use one, write meaning / useWhen / dontUseWhen from its explainer or source page and call save_meme first.

audience.description: Who the video is for: "global" (the English-speaking internet at large) or the viewers' country as a two-letter code (IN, US, GB, BR, MX, JP, KR, PH, NG, DE…). Default: the comp's audience (set on save_beat_sheet). Candidates and library hits local to another country are left out.

force.description: Refetch even when the last refresh is under 6 hours old.

queries.description: Extra YouTube searches for this video's topic (at most 4), e.g. ["Dhurandhar meme"]; only used when the refresh goes online.

query.description: Only return candidates whose name or explainer contains this text.

provider.description: Only return candidates from this provider (kym, imgflip, reddit, youtube, klipy, giphy).

tools.name: save_meme
tools.description: @funny meme brain: saves a meme into the library (new, or replacing the entry with the same id), so search_memes can find it and get_meme_media can fetch it. Write meaning, useWhen and dontUseWhen from a real source (the explainer or page from refresh_meme_trends, Know Your Meme, Wikipedia, a Reddit explainer) and list that source in sources — a meme you cannot explain from a source must not be saved as verified. Rules: id kebab-case (derived from the name when omitted); meaning at least 30 characters; at least one useWhen; at least one source url; intent only from the comic intents; each format needs a url (page, video or file) or a yt-dlp query ("ytsearch3:oggy jack juice meme"), with in/out in source seconds for the usable moment and a transcript of what is said in it when there is speech. Writes only the meme library (Documents/Bhippi/Memes), not the project.

crossover.description: For a local (country) meme only: true when it is known well outside its country too (Tunak Tunak Tun, Kacha Badam, Caramelldansen). Needs a source showing its international spread. Crossover memes may be used for any audience.

id.description: Kebab-case id, e.g. "oggy-jack-juice". Default: from the name.

aliases.description: Other names people use, in English, Hinglish (Roman) and Devanagari.

title.description: The film, show, creator or post it comes from.

meaning.description: What the meme means and how people use it, written from the source (at least 30 characters).

dontUseWhen.description: Situations it must not be used in (tragedy, wrong tone, a misread).

url.description: A page, video (YouTube…) or direct file URL.

query.description: A yt-dlp search when there is no fixed URL, e.g. "ytsearch3:oggy jack juice meme".

in.description: Source seconds where the usable moment starts.

transcript.description: What is said in the clip (so it can echo the host's words).

provider.description: youtube, kym, klipy, giphy, imgflip, reddit…

region.description: global when the English-speaking internet at large knows it; otherwise the two-letter code of the country whose internet it comes from (IN, BR, MX, JP, KR, PH, NG…). A local meme is only offered to that country's viewers.

language.description: What is said in it: an ISO 639-1 code (en, hi, pt, es, ja, ko, tl…), hinglish, or none (no speech).

firstSeen.description: ISO date it first trended, when known.

sources.description: Where the meaning came from (at least one).

verified.description: Default true: the meaning was written from the listed source. False keeps it out of automatic placement.

tools.name: get_meme_media
tools.description: @funny meme brain: fetches one format of a library meme — a direct download, or yt-dlp for a page/video URL or a search query — cut to its moment (in/out, source seconds; keyframes forced at the cuts), caches it under Documents/Bhippi/Memes/media, and imports it into the project's "Memes" folder with commentary provenance. Returns assetId, and in/out within the imported file (already cut, so in is 0) plus hasAudio, ready for place_clip or a meme_cutaway move. The same format and cut come from the cache on the next call. Keep meme clips short (0.6–4 s is typical; at most 120 s). GATHER phase.

format.description: Index into the meme's formats. Default: the best for a cutaway (a clip with sound, a clip, a GIF, a sound, a sticker, a still).

formatType.description: Or the first format of this type.

in.description: Source seconds to start the cut (default: the format's own in).

out.description: Source seconds to end the cut (default: the format's own out).

force.description: Download again even when a cached cut exists.

sceneIndex.description: Storyboard scene this media is for; the file is attached to that planned shot.

tools.name: find_receipt
tools.description: @funny receipts researcher: finds the exact moment someone said something in a YouTube video, from the video's captions, without downloading any video. Searches YouTube with yt-dlp (`query`), reads each result's captions (manual Hindi/English first, else the original-language auto captions; cached per video in Documents/Bhippi/Receipts/captions, so a repeat search is instant) and fuzzy-matches `quote` across scripts: a Roman Hinglish quote finds Devanagari captions and the other way round ("Modi se achcha ek gadha better hai" finds मोदी से अच्छा एक गधा बेटर है). Returns candidates best first — url, title, channel, start/end in source seconds (padded 0.3 s), the caption text matched, a 0–1 score — each with `download`: the download_online_media arguments {url, startTime, endTime} that fetch only that moment. Check the title/channel/text of the best one before downloading; scores under 0.7 are near misses. Requests run one at a time and HTTP 429s from YouTube are waited out, so a search takes 10–60 s. Read-only; any phase. Then download_online_media {url, startTime, endTime} (GATHER) and use the clip as a `receipt` move with word captions.

query.description: What to search YouTube for: who said it and where ("KK Create Dhruv Rathee podcast", "Rahul Gandhi press conference vote chori H files"), or one YouTube URL to search in.

quote.description: The words as they were said, in Roman Hinglish, English or Devanagari. Shorter and exact beats long and paraphrased.

channel.description: Keep to videos by this channel or uploader (matched loosely: "KK Create" matches "Learn By KK Create").

lang.description: Caption language to read ("hi", "en"). Default: Hindi, then English.

tools.name: search_sfx
tools.description: @funny sound library search. Searches, best first: the built-in procedural sounds (whoosh, impact, chime, pop, riser, and the @funny kinds boom = vine boom, scratch = record scratch, bleep = censor tone, swish, ding = bell, glitch — ids sfx-proc-<kind>, no download), the curated CC0 seed pack, and every sound fetched before. Names match in English, Hinglish and Devanagari ("vine boom", "bruhhh", "dhamaka", "धमाका", "घंटी"). With `online: true` it also asks Freesound (CC0 only; needs the user's Freesound key in Settings), Openverse (keyless Creative Commons audio, much of it from Freesound) and Myinstants (meme sound names; user uploads of copyrighted audio, licence unknown — use only as a short commentary sting, prefer built-in or CC0). Every hit carries its id, licence, credit, duration, score and reasons. Read-only; any phase. Pick one and place it with place_sfx.

query.description: What the sound is, in any script: a name ("vine boom", "bruh", "sad violin"), a kind ("record scratch", "airhorn") or a Hinglish word ("dhamaka", "ghanti").

tags.description: Only sounds carrying at least one of these tags (e.g. ["meme"], ["transition"], ["censor"]). A tag-only search lists them.

online.description: Also search Freesound (with the user's key), Openverse and Myinstants (default false).

tools.name: place_sfx
tools.description: @funny: places one sound at `at` (timeline seconds) on the comp's SFX audio track (found or made), labelled audioType sfx, in one undo step, and returns its clipId. Give exactly one of: `kind` (a built-in: whoosh, impact, chime, pop, riser, boom, scratch, bleep, swish, ding, glitch), `id` (from search_sfx; a library sample is downloaded once, trimmed of silence, loudness-normalised to -16 LUFS and imported into the SFX bin), or `query` (picks the best local match, else searches online; Myinstants uploads are skipped unless allowCopyrighted). Default levels sit under the voice: built-ins by kind (boom -14 dB, whoosh/swish/ding -16, bleep/glitch -18, scratch -20), samples -14 dB (-10 for meme/voice sounds like "bruh"); pass `db` only for a deliberate hit. Timing: a meme sound lands on the punchline word's end (+0-150 ms); a whoosh or swish starts ~0.2-0.3 s before the cut or entry it leads into; a pop or ding on the frame a sticker or text appears. The same sound at most 3 times per video; 6-12 sounds a minute in high-energy stretches. For a bleep over a word, use roast_move bleep (it trims the tone to the word). Returns the licence and credit line for the description's credits.

at.description: Timeline seconds the sound starts on.

id.description: A library id from search_sfx (sfx-proc-<kind>, a seed id, fs-…, ov-…, mi-…).

query.description: Find and place the best match in one step (any script).

tags.description: With query: only sounds carrying one of these tags.

online.description: With query: search online when nothing local fits (default true).

allowCopyrighted.description: With query: allow a Myinstants upload (rights unknown). Default false.

db.description: Gain in dB (-60 to 6); defaults sit 10-20 dB under the voice.

note.description: What the sound marks, shown in the clip name (e.g. "punchline", "card lands").

tools.name: cutout_image
tools.description: Cut a person (or any subject) out of a photo or one video frame with BiRefNet (MIT, local GPU; the model downloads on first use, ~450 MB general / ~890 MB portrait) and import the RGBA PNG into the "Cutouts" bin. The edge is cleaned (islands and haze removed, 1 px choke, foreground colour re-estimated under hair, green screens despilled). For the side_cutout sticker look, stroke adds a white outline (strokePx is its thickness when the cut-out is shown 1080 px tall, default 8), shadow a soft drop shadow; the canvas is padded so neither is clipped, and a side the frame edge cuts through stays a straight edge with no stroke. With several people in the frame, pass region around the one you want. Returns assetId (place it with side_cutout or place_clip), bbox of the subject in the source frame (0–1), coverage, and the PNG size. Look at the result before relying on its edge.

assetId.description: Image or video asset to cut from.

clipId.description: A media clip instead of an asset; the frame defaults to the middle of what the clip shows.

path.description: A file on disk that is not imported yet (e.g. a download path).

time.description: Source seconds of the video frame to cut from (default: middle of the clip or asset).

model.description: general (default) for anything; portrait for people with loose hair.

stroke.description: Bake a white sticker outline in (default false).

strokePx.description: Outline thickness when the cut-out is shown 1080 px tall (default 8; 6–10 reads as a sticker).

shadow.description: Bake a soft drop shadow in (default false).

region.description: [x, y, width, height] in frame fractions: only the subject inside is cut out. Use it to pick one person from a group.

choke.description: Pixels to pull the edge in (default 1).

crop.description: Crop to the subject plus room for the stroke and shadow (default true); false keeps the full frame.

sceneIndex.description: Storyboard scene this media is for; the file is attached to that planned shot.

tools.name: detect_faces
tools.description: Find and track faces in a video span (or a still) with YuNet (OpenCV Zoo, MIT; CPU, no GPU; 230 KB model fetched on first use). Faces are linked across frames by overlap, so each track is one person. Returns FaceTrack[]: {id, frames:[{t (source seconds), x, y, width, height (0–1 frame fractions), score, mouth:{x, y} (midpoint of the mouth corners)}]} — the path for head_paste and the mouth box for bleep covers. A span defaults to the clip's source range (or 10 s of an asset); at most 3600 frames per call.

clipId.description: A media clip; the span defaults to what the clip shows.

tools.name: key_green_screen
tools.description: Detect a chroma-green backdrop and key it. Samples frames of each clip's source range (FFmpeg + a border/full-frame chroma test, no model), reports greenShare (0–1 share of sampled frames standing on a green backdrop) and the backdrop's colour, and — for every clip whose greenShare is at least minShare — attaches the keylight effect (screen colour, gain and balance solved from the measured backdrop, 50 % spill suppression) exactly as edit_effect would, all in one undo step; an existing keylight on the clip is updated rather than duplicated. Keylight renders in preview and export. Use all: true to scan every video clip of the comp (compId or the active one). After keying, look at a frame for fringe or holes in dark clothes and put something behind the host.

clipId.description: One video clip to check and key.

all.description: Check every enabled video clip of the comp (clips named like a background plate are skipped).

compId.description: Comp for all: true (default: the active comp).

minShare.description: Key a clip when at least this share of its frames is green (default 0.5).

dryRun.description: Measure and report only; attach nothing.

tools.name: save_beat_sheet
tools.description: Saves the beat sheet of a roast recording on the comp (@funny step 2): each sentence labelled setup / punchline / claim / quote / reference / question / emotion / callback / profanity / cta / filler, with a comic intent, entities and echo words. Checked and tidied first: beats sorted, overlaps trimmed, ids made unique, unknown kinds and intents dropped. Pass the transcript's timeline words to fill punchAt (end of a punchline's last word), profanity spans (Hindi/Hinglish in Roman and Devanagari, English, YouTube's [ __ ]) and echo words the beats leave out. Returns counts by kind and the profanity found (bleep candidates).

audience.description: Who the video is for, which decides the memes: "global" (the English-speaking internet at large) or the viewers' country as a two-letter code (IN for Hindi/Hinglish, BR, MX, JP, KR, PH, US, GB…). Default auto: detected from the beats' words (Devanagari/Hinglish → IN, Hangul → KR, Japanese → JP, Thai → TH, otherwise global) unless the user already set it. Set it when the user says who the video is for, or when the speech is clearly another country's (Brazilian Portuguese → BR, Mexican Spanish → MX).

text.description: The words spoken, as transcribed (Devanagari and/or Roman).

intent.description: One comic intent: betrayal, exposed, chase, clueless, fake-sad, hype, cringe, shock, awkward, victory, fail, sarcasm, confusion, denial, flex, disgust, suspense, wholesome, rage, dead, money, lie, smell, dance, agree, disagree, ignore, overreact, plot-twist, hypocrisy, cheating, poison, crazy, proud, scared, bye.

echo.description: Concrete words a meme could repeat ("zeher", "juice", "German shepherd").

punchAt.description: Timeline seconds the punchline lands (end of its last word).

words.description: Optional: the transcript's words in timeline seconds, to fill punchAt, profanity and echo words.

tools.name: roast_move
tools.description: Makes one comedy move on the timeline and appends it to the comp's roast EDL, as one undo step. Moves: meme_cutaway {assetId, in?, fit?: fill|fit|blur-fill, keepAudio?, duckHostDb?, entry?: cut|whip|zoom, memeId?} full-frame on the Memes lane, the host muted while the meme's own sound plays, blur-fill by default for vertical sources, 0.6-4 s; receipt {assetId, in?, fit?, captions?, words?: [{text,start,end}] in the clip's source seconds, label?} with word-by-word captions and a *NAME label; side_cutout {assetId, side: left|right, heightPct? (55), enter?: slide|pop} slides in from off-frame with overshoot; host_on_bg {bgAssetId | color, hostClipId?, in?} needs a roto matte or key on the host; keyword_pop {text (1-3 words), style: memeImpact|roundedPop|labelStar|fireCta, position?: top|center|bottom|behind, color?}; emoji_pop {emoji, x?, y?, sizePct?}; sticker {text, shape?, color?, x?, y?}; overlay_fx {fx: fx-money-rain|fx-speed-lines|fx-hearts-burst|fx-embers|fx-spotlight|fx-confetti|fx-smoke-question, tint?}; card {template: roast-article-card|roast-then-now|roast-fact-strip|roast-profile-card|roast-poster-card|roast-sticker-badge|roast-title-card|roast-cta-fire, params, placement?}; title_card {text, photoAssetId?, accent?}; cta {text}; zoom_punch {clipId?, scale? (112-140), ease?: snap|slow}; shake {clipId?, intensityPx?, frames?}; whip {clipId?} across the host cut nearest at; bw_freeze {clipId?, freeze?}; label {text, x?, y?, path?: [{t,x,y}] with t seconds from at}; head_paste {headAssetId, path: [{t,x,y,scale,rotation?}]}; bleep {from, to, cover?: emoji|blur|none, mouth?}; music_sting {assetId, in?, db?, fadeOut?, snapToBeat?}; sfx {cue}. Every move plays its default sound unless sfx is given (null: silent): a swish for slides, cards and whips, a pop for text, a boom for a still meme, an impact for a shake, a scratch for a freeze, a ding for a CTA. Clips it makes are named roast:<id>.

event.description: A RoastEvent: the move's fields plus id? (e1, e2... when left out), at (timeline seconds; for memes the punchline word's end), duration (seconds; the move's default when left out), why (one sentence; required for meme_cutaway, receipt and side_cutout), beatId?, sfx? ({kind|id|assetId, offset?, db?} or null), provenance?, alternates?.

beats.description: Optional beat times (timeline seconds) for music_sting snapping; the plan's analysed music is used when left out.

tools.name: validate_roast_edl
tools.description: Checks a roast EDL without touching the timeline: unknown asset or clip ids, events outside the comp, overlapping full-frame cutaways, a missing why on meme_cutaway / receipt / side_cutout, host_on_bg without a matte or key, the same sound more than 3 times, durations out of bounds. Runs the plan on a copy and returns the Edit DNA it would have, its dead zones (host-only stretches over 8 s) and the findings against the @funny band. Run it before apply_roast_edl.

replace.description: Judge the plan as replacing the comp's current roast plan (default: merged into it, same ids replaced).

tools.name: apply_roast_edl
tools.description: Assembles a roast EDL on the timeline in one undo step. Validates first and applies nothing if any event has an error. Events with ids already applied are taken back and made again (re-applying never doubles clips); replace:true takes back the whole previous plan first. Stores the plan, what each event made and the resulting Edit DNA on the comp, and returns the report: errors, warnings, dead zones and findings against the @funny band.

beats.description: Beat times, timeline seconds (music_sting snapping, on-beat share).

tools.name: edit_dna
tools.description: Measures the Edit DNA of the timeline (cuts and cuts per minute, median shot, longest host-only stretch with no cut or event, on-screen events, SFX per minute, music coverage, memes, text events, on-beat share with beats) or of a video file (source: file, path; scene cuts, SFX transients, music, beat alignment, unkeyed green share), and compares it with the @funny band: dead zones over 8 s block hand-back; slow opening minutes, SFX out of 6-12 a minute and a constant music bed are fixes.

path.description: The video file to measure (source: file).

beats.description: Beat times, timeline seconds, for the on-beat share.

tools.name: plugin_sdk_reference
tools.description: The Bhippi plugin SDK reference: how a plugin page is built, the bhippi.* API (project, comp, tool, selection, playhead, storage, toast, chat, on, expose), permissions and the rules plugins follow. Read it before writing or changing a plugin.

tools.name: list_plugins
tools.description: List the user's Bhippi plugins (panels/automations built in the Plugin Maker): id, name, description, whether enabled / shown as a panel / running in the background, permissions and the actions each running plugin exposes.

query.description: Optional search text

tools.name: get_plugin
tools.description: One plugin in full, including its HTML source and permissions. Omit id for the plugin open in the Plugin Maker.

tools.name: save_plugin
tools.description: Create a Bhippi plugin, or change one (pass its id). A plugin is ONE HTML document with inline <script>/<style> that runs sandboxed in a panel and reaches the editor only through the bhippi SDK (see plugin_sdk_reference). Saving reloads it; the previous version is kept. Then call plugin_logs to check it loaded clean.

id.description: The plugin to change. Omit to create a new one (the id is made from the name).

name.description: Short name for the panel tab (required for a new plugin).

html.description: The whole page. Required for a new plugin; omit to keep the current page (e.g. to change only permissions).

permissions.description: What the plugin may use. Reading tools are always allowed.

tools.description: Bhippi tools it may run via bhippi.tool(). "*" = all non-sensitive tools; sensitive ones (run_command, write_file, edit_file, install_local_model, deletes) must be named.

network.description: Hosts it may fetch/WebSocket to, e.g. "api.example.com", "*.example.com", "http://127.0.0.1:5678". Empty = no network.

chat.description: May send messages to the Bhippi AI chat (bhippi.chat).

background.description: Keep running while hidden, for automations that react to events or expose actions.

showAsPanel.description: Show it as a tab in the Plugins panel (default true for a new plugin).

note.description: What changed, kept with the previous version.

tools.name: plugin_scaffold
tools.description: Start a new plugin from a template: writes its draft (manifest.json, spec.md, index.html, app.js, style.css) and installs it so the preview shows it. Templates: panel (a UI panel), background (an automation with a small status log), action (offers Bhippi AI an action via bhippi.expose), panel-actions (a panel that also exposes actions). Then write spec.md, then the code.

id.description: Optional id (lower-case letters, digits, - and _); made from the name when omitted.

tools.name: plugin_list_files
tools.description: The files in a plugin's draft with their sizes. A plugin that has no draft yet gets one made from its installed page.

id.description: The plugin id. Omit for the plugin open in the Plugin Maker.

tools.name: plugin_read_file
tools.description: Read one file of a plugin's draft.

id.description: The plugin id. Omit for the plugin open in the Plugin Maker.

file.description: A file name in the draft: letters, digits, - _ . only, no folders (manifest.json, spec.md, index.html, app.js, style.css, …).

tools.name: plugin_write_file
tools.description: Create or replace one file of a plugin's draft (whole contents). Nothing runs until plugin_save. Code and text: .html .js .css .json .md .svg .txt .gltf. Assets (bundled into the page, read with bhippi.asset): .png .jpg .webp .gif .avif .glb .bin .woff .woff2 .ttf .otf .wav .mp3 .ogg .m4a .mp4 .webm .wasm, sent as base64. To copy a project media file in, use plugin_add_asset; for three.js, plugin_add_library.

id.description: The plugin id. Omit for the plugin open in the Plugin Maker.

file.description: A file name in the draft: letters, digits, - _ . only, no folders (manifest.json, spec.md, index.html, app.js, style.css, texture.png, …).

content.description: The whole file. For an asset (binary) file: its bytes as base64.

encoding.description: How content is written: utf8 (default) or base64 (required for binary assets).

tools.name: plugin_add_library
tools.description: Copy a library Bhippi ships into a plugin's draft (plugins cannot load code from a CDN). The copy is checked against the pinned hash and becomes a draft file, e.g. three.min.js; add <script src="three.min.js"></script> to index.html before app.js. Omit library to list them (three: three.js 3D with OrbitControls, TransformControls, GLTFLoader, GLTFExporter).

id.description: The plugin id. Omit for the plugin open in the Plugin Maker.

tools.name: plugin_add_asset
tools.description: Copy one of the project's media files (a picture, model, font, sound, clip or wasm; up to 8 MB) into a plugin's draft as an asset. The page reads it with bhippi.asset(name) (a blob URL), bhippi.assetBytes(name) or . It is bundled at plugin_save.

id.description: The plugin id. Omit for the plugin open in the Plugin Maker.

path.description: Absolute path of a project media file (get_project lists them) or a file in the project's folder.

name.description: The asset's name in the draft (keeps a known ending such as .png or .glb). Default: the file's own name.

tools.name: plugin_delete_file
tools.description: Delete one file from a plugin's draft (manifest.json and index.html cannot be deleted).

id.description: The plugin id. Omit for the plugin open in the Plugin Maker.

file.description: A file name in the draft: letters, digits, - _ . only, no folders (manifest.json, spec.md, index.html, app.js, style.css, …).

tools.name: plugin_validate
tools.description: Check a plugin's draft without running it (free, instant): manifest fields, spec.md sections, files index.html references, no remote scripts, every bhippi.tool() name is a real tool, permissions match the tools the code calls (none missing, none unused, no '*' without need), acceptance checks present, theme variables and error handling used, sizes. Returns problems and warnings to fix.

id.description: The plugin id. Omit for the plugin open in the Plugin Maker.

tools.name: plugin_test
tools.description: Run the saved plugin in a hidden sandboxed frame against a SCRATCH COPY of the project (the real project is never touched): waits for it to load, collects console errors and refused calls, runs its bhippi.test() acceptance checks, and counts the edits it made to the copy. Returns the report and the Plugin Maker Judge's score (0–100, pass 80) with fixes. plugin_save first.

id.description: The plugin id. Omit for the plugin open in the Plugin Maker.

waitMs.description: How long to let it settle before the checks run (default 1500, max 8000).

tools.name: plugin_screenshot
tools.description: Pictures of the saved plugin's panel at narrow (320 px) and wide (480 px) widths, rendered in the sandbox against a scratch copy of the project, for a look at layout, overflow, contrast and styling. The images come back with the result.

id.description: The plugin id. Omit for the plugin open in the Plugin Maker.

widths.description: Panel widths in px (default [320, 480], at most 3, each 240–1200).

tools.name: plugin_save
tools.description: Bundle the draft into the installed plugin: index.html with the app.js/style.css it references inlined, the manifest's name, icon, description and permissions applied. The preview reloads. The previous version is kept (last 10).

id.description: The plugin id. Omit for the plugin open in the Plugin Maker.

note.description: What changed, for the version history.

tools.name: plugin_examples
tools.description: Reviewed example plugins to learn from: with no id, the list; with an id, its full source (manifest, spec, code).

tools.name: plugin_tool_catalog
tools.description: Every Bhippi tool a plugin can call through bhippi.tool(), one line each, marked read (always allowed) or sensitive (must be named in permissions). Filter with query. tool_help gives one tool's full parameters.

tools.name: plugin_logs
tools.description: Read a plugin's console: console.log/warn/error lines, uncaught errors, and every bhippi call it made with its result. Use after save_plugin to confirm the plugin loaded, and to debug it. Omit id for the plugin open in the Plugin Maker.

tools.name: call_plugin_action
tools.description: Run an action a running plugin exposes with bhippi.expose() (listed in the context's plugins.actions and by list_plugins). The plugin must be running: open in the Plugin Maker, a visible panel, or a background plugin.

args.description: Arguments, as the action's params schema describes

tools.name: show_plugin
tools.description: Show a plugin as a tab in the Plugins panel (panel true), or take it out of the panel (panel false). Omit id for the plugin open in the Plugin Maker.

tools.name: delete_plugin
tools.description: Delete a plugin with its saved data. Only when the user asks for that plugin to be deleted.
